Loss function.d: A formula that turns a model's mistake on an example into a single number: zero is perfect, bigger is worse. Training tries to make this number small.

Learning rate.d: How big a step gradient descent takes each time it adjusts the weights. Too small and training is slow; too large and the loss bounces around or explodes.

Epoch.d: One complete pass through all the training data during training.

Batch.d: A small group of training examples processed together. The model averages their gradients and makes one weight update per batch.

Overfitting.d: When a model learns the quirks and noise of its training data so closely that it does worse on new examples. Training loss keeps falling while validation loss rises.

Underfitting.d: When a model is too simple, or trained too little, to capture the real pattern. It does badly on both training and new data.

Training set.d: The part of a dataset the model actually learns from: its weights are adjusted on these examples.

Validation set.d: Data held back from training and checked during development, to compare models, tune settings and spot overfitting.

Test set.d: Data kept locked away until the very end and used once for an honest final score. Never used for training or tuning.

Data leakage.d: When information from the validation or test data sneaks into training, for example through duplicates or time order, so scores look better than real-world performance.

Data bias.d: When a dataset is systematically unrepresentative of the real world a model will be used in, through sampling, history, labelling or measurement. The model learns the bias.

Data labelling.d: Attaching the correct answer (label) to each example in a dataset, usually by people following written guidelines. Also called annotation.

Cosine similarity.d: A measure of how closely two vectors point in the same direction: the dot product divided by the product of their lengths. 1 means same direction, around 0 means unrelated.

Semantic search.d: Search by meaning rather than exact words: the query and documents are turned into embeddings and the closest documents are returned.

Embedding model.d: A model whose job is to turn text (or images) into embedding vectors for search, clustering and RAG. Anthropic does not make one; providers include Voyage AI and open-source models.
